newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly forms women's health unit.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly forms women's health unit.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said Monday it formed a new business unit to provide greater emphasis on women's health.

Among the responsibilities of the new unit will be the approval and commercialization of Evista, which is among the first in a new class of drugs called selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs).

Lilly said SERMs may be an alternative to hormone replacement therapy in the prevention of postmenopausal health risks, including osteoporosis. Evista has been submitted for regulatory approval in the United States and more than 20 other countries.
Gino Santini has been named president, women's health business unit, reporting to Sidney Taurel, president and chief operating officer of Lilly.
"As Evista rapidly approaches the marketplace, it requires dedicated focus," Taurel said in a statement.
